newsitem.title: LATVIA: LATVIA-GRINDEX H1 AFTER-TAX PROFIT 0.5 MLN LATS.
newsitem.headline: LATVIA-GRINDEX H1 AFTER-TAX PROFIT 0.5 MLN LATS.

text.p: Grindex, one of the two biggest pharmaceutical firms in Latvia, on Monday said its half-year after-tax profit was 500,000 lats on sales of 4.1 million lats.
"Grindex's turnover during the first six month of 1997 has grown by about one million lats compared to the corresponding period of 1996," manager Valdis Jekabsons told Reuters.
Grindex registered a 1996 after-tax profit of 160,000 lats.
The company, currently in the final stage of its sell-off, sees 1997 turnover of 10.5 million lats against 8.03 million lats last year.
"We plan to earn nine percent of 1997 turnover in profit," Jekabsons added.
Some 25 percent of the company's produce are active substances for medicines, most of which is exported to Japan and 60 percent of its output is ready prepared medications.
"These are currently mainly substances for anti-cancer drugs and Japan is testing a Grindex patented drug for cardio-vascular diseases," Jekabsons said.
"The results are expected in 2003," he said.
Another 16 percent of Grindex's turnover is generated by distibuting the medicines of other poducers.
"I am satisfied with the distribution of our markets as we have a very good spread," Jekabsons said.
"We sell 34 percent in Latvia, 10 percent in Estonia and Lithuania combined, two to 25 percent in Japan and 30 percent in Russia and CIS countries," he said.
